back: The number of subordinates reporting directly to one manager or supervisor.
The line through which instructions pass down the hierarchy and information passes up.
The levels of authority in a business, from senior managers to workers.
Many levels, narrow spans, close supervision, slow communication, more managers (cost), more promotion steps.
Few levels, wide spans, faster communication, lower cost, more responsibility for workers, less supervision.

front: Part-time employees: one advantage, one disadvantage?
back: Can be matched to busy periods (lower cost); may be less committed and harder to communicate with.

front: Home working: one advantage, one disadvantage?
back: Saves office space and travel time; harder to supervise and communicate.

front: What happens when a level of management is removed (delayering)?
back: Fewer levels, wider spans of control, faster communication and lower cost, but heavier workloads and fewer promotion posts.
